title: Goldreich–Levin active-set invariant
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:{-1,1}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $\tau$ be a rational number with $0<\tau\le 1$, let $k\in\mathbb N$, and let $A$ be a family of subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The invariant requires that every $S\in A$ be contained in the first $k$ coordinates; that every set of coordinates $U$ whose Fourier coefficient for $f$ has absolute value at least $\tau$ has its prefix-frequency part at level $k$ in $A$; and, for every $k>0$ and every $S\in A$, the restricted Fourier weight of $f$ on the free-frequency part associated with $S$ and the first $k$ coordinates is strictly greater than $\tau^2/4$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on $n$ coordinates with values in the signs
$A$ is a finite family of coordinate subsets
caveat: The formal statement uses upstream notions of prefix coordinates, prefix frequency, free frequency part, and restricted Fourier weight whose definitions are not provided in the payload; their exact mathematical meanings cannot be recovered here.
